items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: Up on the sixth floor was the A&R Studios, run by Phil Ramone, who is a famous A&R man today. He’s Barbra Streisand’s A&R man or something. He was just another genius in those days.

ctx.x: We’re all playing the same notes. This guy had to show that he knew something about music, so he hit the intercom button he says, “All right guys,” he says, “we’ve got to straighten something out.” He says, “The third flute there’s a couple of bad notes at Letter C.” We’re all playing unison, the same note. So I look at Phil, and he looks at me, and we both looked at Romeo, and these are the most famous doublers in New York City.
